tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

items.description: The whole plan, in order (1–12 steps); replaces the previous list.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

# v0.1 reconstruction: kernel brief (shared by every agent of the kernel phase)

## Context

- Repository `/Users/guygouri/Devlab/ernlang/ern`, branch `reference/memory-model-v0`. Lake project `formal/`
  (Lean 4, no Mathlib). Build from `formal/` with `~/.elan/bin/lake`.
- Normative source: `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md`. Its header lists the amended clauses;
  clause numbers are those of v0, with the new item §63.9. v0 is history: never cite it.
- The user's arbitrations, verbatim: `SP/v01/arbitration.md`, where
  `SP=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guygouri-Devlab-ernlang-ern/c986905c-e900-4fd9-bebc-4a3ce7ebb180/scratchpad/ref`.
  Read the clauses you touch in the v0.1 file and the arbitration file before editing.
- Previous obligation map (v0 era, for orientation only): `SP/table-final.md`.

## Hard rules (in addition to AGENTS.md)

- No `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom`, `native_decide`, `noncomputable`, `set_option`. No warnings.
- Every constant's axioms must be within {propext, Quot.sound}. `Classical.choice` is NOT allowed. Avoid
  `Classical`, `by_contra` on non-decidable props, `Decidable.byContradiction` on classical instances,
  `simp` lemmas that pull `Classical.choice` (check if unsure with `#print axioms` in a scratch file
  under `SP/`).
- Every def/theorem docstring cites the clause it formalizes (`§63.9`, `§69.2`, ...). Module headers that
  name the spec file must name `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md`.
- Everything in English. Do not commit; do not touch git state (no stash, checkout, reset).
- Never weaken a statement, never add an unjustified hypothesis, never change a definition to make a

# ERN — Memory Model Specification v0.1

**Edition v0.1 — corrective candidate, not yet validated**

Modified clauses, relative to v0 (each change is justified by a defect found while formalizing v0):

- §36: `MetaRight` governs authorities over existing storage, not the fresh allocation of `alloc`; §36 and §71.2 contradicted each other.
- §40: `RootHeld` restricted to usable root places, as in §49.7; the two clauses differed on unusable root places.
- §47: the ownership graph of statics is acyclic; a static ownership cycle made §57 false in the initial state.
- §51: a valid origin is an active origin; "valid" was undefined there.
- §57: definition of I5, which v0 named without defining.
- §59: "access operations" are O9–O11; read as all operations, §59 contradicted §69.
- §60.1: a valid origin chain is an active one, read through §44.
- §63.4: the active derived authorities covering the source from outside are named, and the authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right are exempt; without this exemption no value could be moved through a derived authority.
- §63.9 (new): the destination is usable in the resulting state; without it an accepted transfer could create an ownership cycle and break §49.8 and §57.
- §69.2 and §70.3: the same exemption as §63.4, and rejection when an authority made inactive by the step keeps an active descendant; without it an accepted step left an active authority with an inactive origin.
- §71.2: the provider is a usable place; v0 did not require it to exist.
- §74 and §75: each `pin` installs an obligation of fresh identity and `unpin` ends one designated obligation; per-leaf pin flags let an `unpin` lift a pin installed by another `pin`.
- §76.6: the reading of the precondition (whole kernel state, `ArenaInv` of the new entry, resulting state); v0 admitted several readings with different verdicts.
- §78.3: restricted to anchors covering a leaf of the administered storage; as written, its second sentence was false.
- §82.2: address and provenance of a pointer to a region whose leaves all have zero physical size; v0 decided no address for that region.
- §86: the last sentence is rewritten; as written, it was false, since `reset` and `issue` leave a recycled leaf `Init` and readable.

**Higher normative authority:** *ERN — Language Charter v0* (October 27, 2026).  
This specification defines the normative rules of ERN's memory model. Technical names (`derive`, `transfer`, `issue`, etc.) designate **abstract semantic operations**; they do not constitute syntax decisions.

## Validation and Revision Procedure

This edition has been validated and acquires normative authority under the ERN Charter v0. Any subsequent semantic change must identify the clauses concerned, justify the change, and preserve the guarantees of the ERN Charter v0. Formal models and proofs are instruments for verifying this specification, not sources of additional rules. Behaviors not determined within its scope are explicitly identified.

----
## 46. Arenas as Library Administration States

Each entry belongs to the library's abstract state, **separate from kernel state `S₃`**. It has the following fields:

```text
ArenaEntry {
    storage: PlaceId
    internal: AuthorityId
    available: Set<Leaf>
    issued: Set<(Region, AuthorityId)>
}
```

A region is **available if and only if each of its leaves belongs to `available`**; the empty region is always available. Issuance removes the leaves of the issued region from `available`. Reset restores all leaves of the administered storage to that set. The registry and its updates belong to the abstraction contract and create no kernel permissions.

The arena is **live** if `internal` is active. The **arena value** is the place holding `internal`, distinct from the possible owner of `storage`. Administered storage may be local, static, allocated, or issued by another arena, under `newArena` preconditions and applicable invariants. `available` and `issued` remain **in the library's arena entry**.

## 47. Initial State

The kernel's initial state contains only base frame 0 and the declared static storage. Every static leaf has its declared initial state, `Init` or `Uninit`. The roots of static places directly owned by frame 0 have a root `Modify` authority held by that frame; a static may also be owned by another static, in which case its root authority is held by the latter. The ownership graph of statics is acyclic: no static is owned, directly or transitively, by itself. The initial state invents no dynamic allocation, derived authority, or implicit anchor. The initial arena registry belongs to library state and is empty. The initial frame does not exit.

## 48. External Parametric Contract

`K` contains the predicates `DeclaredDisjoint`, `SharedMutable`, `Pinned`, `ExternalDone`, `Deallocable`, `FreeCompat`, and `Satisfiable`. Their obligations are specified in Section 80. `K` can neither fabricate access rights nor remove an obligation of the Charter. The predicate `Invalidates` is not part of this contract.

# VII. Invariants of Reachable States

Machine states are subject to structural, validity, and exclusivity requirements preserved by permitted transitions under their declared external contracts.

## 49. WF3 — Well-Formedness of Frames, Places, and Authorities

`WF3(s)` is a **predicate on state `s`**. It jointly requires:

1. a nonempty, duplicate-free frame stack, every frame having a valid identity and, except for the base frame, a valid parent; frame-parent relations are well-founded;
2. a place structure whose composition links are valid and **acyclic**; every structural part shares its parent's owner and death marker;
3. valid owners of type frame or place, and **well-founded** ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place;
4. footprints consisting exclusively of leaves of existing places;
5. authorities with valid identities and modes, whose existing origins form **acyclic** chains ending at a root authority;
6. `RootChain`: every origin chain of an authority covering a leaf ends at the root of the **same structural root place** as that leaf;
7. `RootHeld`: every usable root place has its active root `Modify` authority, with no origin, held exactly by its owner;
8. holder validity: every active authority is held by a frame present in the stack or by a usable place.

Numerical ordering of identifiers, parent precedence over child in a list, and bounds on generated identifiers may be used **to represent or prove** this well-formedness in a formalization; they are not normative restrictions on place or authority identities. Preservation of `WF3` by a transition is a **required property of transitions**, not an additional clause of the state predicate. `WF3` does not impose any particular physical object layout: that belongs to refinement into the elementary memory machine.

## 50. I1 — Structural Exclusivity

For two active authorities **unrelated by derivation** covering the same leaf, their own modes must both be `Observe`. This rule also applies to leaves identified as `SharedMutable`; their particular mutation is governed by the `writeShared` contract and creates no exception to I1.

Exclusivity of **effective** modes (`effective_exclusive`) is a consequence of I1 and the definition of `effective`, not the definition of I1. On a leaf, two incompatible authorities cannot simultaneously possess incompatible effective rights. The only permitted independent ordinary coexistence is `Observe` / `Observe`.

## 51. I2 — Conservation of Rights

A derived authority covers only a subfootprint of what its origin chain permits and does not elevate its mode. Derivation and splitting restrictions do not allow duplication of an exclusive right over a leaf. Every active authority is linked to a valid origin according to state and reanchoring rules: an origin is **valid** if and only if it is active, so the origin of an active derived authority is active. Partial suspension follows from `effective`.

## 52. I3 — Validity of Anchors and Dependencies

Every explicit anchor of a still-usable place is valid. An operation cannot invalidate an anchor retained by a place that remains usable. Transitive propagation of dependencies from contained values does not change this obligation. Dependencies are not permissions and are insufficient to justify an access.

## 53. I4 — Consumption and Movement

A `Moved` leaf cannot be read as if it still contained its previous value. Moving a value does not preserve two copies of an exclusive authority. Initialization state and authority-exercise state are separate checks.

## 54. Anchor Ordering and Absence of Orphan Rights

`AnchorOrder` and `AnchorOrderHeld` are defined in Section 44. `NoDangling` prohibits an **active** authority from covering a leaf belonging to an unusable place; the invariant does not say that a leaf is initialized. `NoOrphan` requires every active authority held by a place to be connected to a frame in the stack through a **finite, non-repeating chain** of authorities: the first link is held by a live frame, and each active link **structurally covers the entirety** of the place holding the next link. The link need not have an effective mode over that place. `NoOrphan` guarantees neither the exercisability of all stored authorities nor freedom from blocking.

## 55. ArenaInv — Invariant of the Arena Abstraction

`ArenaInv` is an invariant of the **library contract**, not an additional predicate of kernel state. For every live arena:

- `storage` designates an existing, usable place; the footprint of `internal` is exactly the footprint of `storage`;
- `internal` is active, with own mode `Modify`, held by the arena value;
- available leaves and issued regions belong to the administered storage;
- two still-active issuances have disjoint regions; no leaf of a still-issued region simultaneously belongs to `available`;
- every still-issued block authority is a derivative of `internal` complying with exclusivity and validity rules;
- anchor and ownership restrictions are respected.

Arena entries do not, by themselves, constitute an additional storage owner. Two live arenas may cover common leaves when their `internal` authorities are distinct and their effective rights are compatible; no **global** disjointness of arena footprints is imposed.

## 56. Uniqueness of Live Administration

**An authority identity may serve as `internal` for at most one live administrative abstraction**, whether an arena, `HandlePool`, `DataStack`, or another library administrative instance. Before registering a new abstraction, its creation operation must jointly check the absence of that identity from **all relevant registries of live administrations**. Uniqueness concerns the identity of the `internal` authority, not merely possible overlap of footprints: abstractions with distinct `internal` identities are not forbidden merely because their footprints overlap. Library contracts must make the information required for this guard available to the creation operation; checking only an abstraction's own registry is insufficient.

**This guard is not a condition for any safety property in Section 57.** The effective right (Section 43, case 3) already prohibits a second issuance over leaves covered by an active block derived from the same authority. Rather, the guard preserves the **abstraction contract**: without it, simultaneous administration of the same `internal` could cause `reject` instead of `fail`, or reissue a previously released block that the first administration still considers unavailable. It creates neither permissions nor allocations and introduces no general detection of authority cycles. Its physical representation and encapsulation of library registries remain outside the kernel.

## 57. Main Invariant

\[
Inv3 = I1 \land I2 \land I3 \land I4 \land AnchorOrder \land NoDangling
\]

On states reachable from `S3.init statics` under `DDSound(K)`, the kernel guarantees:

\[
WF3 \land Inv3 \land AnchorOrderHeld \land NoOrphan
\]

`ArenaInv` (Section 55) belongs to the library abstraction: it is not included in this main kernel invariant.

**I5:** every pinned leaf, statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (an active pinning obligation, Section 74), belongs to a usable place.

I5, associated with pinned storage, remains a **specialized obligation** of `K.Pinned`, not a clause automatically implied by sequential accesses alone. This property is required for reachable states under the declared assumptions. Its correspondence with allocations and bytes requires the refinement defined below.

# VIII. Definition of Transitions and Management of Authorities

The following operations are abstract transition rules. They distinguish rejection by the discipline, defined failure, and a permitted transition.

# XIV. Arenas and Collective Invalidation — Reference Abstraction

An arena is a **library abstraction**, not a memory-kernel primitive. Operations O17 through O19 are **derived** from operations O1 through O16 and abstraction-specific metadata: `newArena` registers an administration without modifying the kernel; `issue` performs `split` followed by `store` (after checking availability); `reset` performs a `Modify` derivation over all storage—through `derive` or `split`—then `release`, before restoring availability. Their contract below is **normative for the standard-library arena** until Spec 10 takes responsibility for it. It authorizes neither new permissions nor an additional access machine. Arena entries (Section 46) constitute the abstract state of this administration; the guard in Section 56 belongs to its consistency contract. The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and are not defined here.

## 76. O17 — Creation of an Administered Arena

**Preconditions**

1. `storage` is an existing, usable place under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame. It may be local, static, allocated, or a block issued by a previous arena.
2. `internal` is explicitly named by the caller, exists, is active, has own mode `Modify`, and `ExercisableAt(s,internal,Modify)` holds.
3. `internal` is **held by a place**: that place is the arena value; `footprint(internal) = footprint(storage)`.
4. **Unified administration guard (Section 56):** no **live** administrative abstraction, whether an arena or a library instance such as a handle pool, already uses this `internal` identity. The relevant registries of library administrations are consulted before registration. Two distinct identities may cover common leaves: this is not in itself grounds for rejection.
5. All leaves of the arena value holding `internal` are already `Init`; construction does not initialize them implicitly.
6. Dependency, holder, storage, and administration relations respect, in the resulting state, `WF3`, I1, `AnchorOrder`, and `AnchorOrderHeld` over the whole kernel state, and the new entry satisfies `ArenaInv` (Section 55).

**`ok` effect:** A live entry `{storage, internal, available, issued}` is added; the initial `available` set represents the administered storage, and `issued` is initially empty. Registering the entry fabricates no place, access right, or `Init` state. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

The identity of `internal`, not the index of `storage`, is the key to preventing duplication of live administrations. No global constraint requires footprints of live arenas to be pairwise disjoint.

## 77. O18 — Issuing an Arena Block

**Static preconditions**

1. The `arena` entry exists and is live; `internal` is active. `MetaRight` requires exercisable `Modify` over the arena value holding `internal` (Section 36). Mutation of metadata through `writeShared` alone does not satisfy this condition.
2. `region` belongs to the administered storage; `destination` is a usable **leaf** holding no active authority; the destination can legally receive the block value in mode `Modify`. The fact that `destination` is already `Init` is not in itself grounds for rejection, in accordance with O8.2.
   **Local self-blocking prevention: leaf `destination` is not in `region`, including when the region is declared available.** This condition is static and is checked before an availability `fail`.
3. Applicable **static** validity and non-escape restrictions for the destination are satisfied. The `AnchorOrder` check depending on the new anchor is performed on the **simulated resulting state**, after the availability check described in point 4; it cannot turn an unavailable issuance (`fail`) into `reject`.

**Availability and exercisability checks**

4. If static conditions hold but **at least one leaf of `region` does not belong to `available`**, the operation produces **`fail` and leaves the entire state unchanged**. The empty region is always available. An unavailable region does not permit a prior static rejection to be bypassed.
5. If the region is available, the effective mode of `internal` on that region must permit `Modify`; otherwise the outcome is `reject`.
6. The simulated result must satisfy `AnchorOrderHeld` **in the resulting state**; moreover, **in that resulting state, `destination` must remain under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame**, in accordance with O8.5. Issuance into a value with a longer lifetime than a local anchor is not made valid merely by storing it in the caller.

**`ok` effect:** A block authority of fresh identity, derived from `internal` and of mode `Modify`, is issued for the region; it is held by `destination`, which receives the corresponding anchor. The leaves of the region leave `available`, and the issuance is added to `issued` with its authority. **Only leaf `destination` becomes `Init`**; no other leaf of the arena value changes initialization. Previous issuances remain intact and valid. Issuance does not automatically install anchors on third-party values: they must use their lawful dependency mechanisms.

**Outcomes:** `ok`, `fail` (region unavailable after static validation), `reject` (static rule, effective right, or anchoring not satisfied). The destination may be a leaf of the arena value itself: its initialization then constitutes **an explicit write to that destination**, not implicit initialization of the entire arena value's metadata.

## 78. O19 — Collective Arena Reset

**Preconditions**

1. The entry exists and is live. **`MetaRight(s,arena)` requires exercisable `Modify` over the arena value**, in accordance with Section 36. `writeShared` over metadata alone, even when legal, does not replace such exercise. `internal` and the arena's other restrictions remain valid.
2. **No active authority derived from `internal` covers a leaf of the administered storage.** A derived authority with an empty footprint does not, by itself, block `reset`.
3. No still-usable place depends, directly or transitively, on an anchor in the **strict origin subtree of `internal`** (`internal` itself is excluded) that covers a leaf of the administered storage. Under precondition 2 and invariant I3, this condition follows from the absence of active descendants covering the storage, and remains explicit in the abstraction contract. Validity obligations of other nested arenas remain satisfied.

**`ok` effect:** All **leaves** of the administered storage become available again, and the issuance list is cleared under the arena contract. No still-active derived authority covering those leaves may remain, by precondition 2; an empty-footprint derivative may remain active without designating any recycled leaf. **No leaf is made `Init` by `reset`**, including in the arena value. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

Safe reuse after `reset` requires that previous issuances **covering recycled leaves**, and the dependencies on which their validity rests, have effectively ceased preventing their reuse. Any active empty-footprint derivatives cover none of those leaves. A historically issued region does not remain permanently unavailable solely for that reason.

# XV. Transitive Dependencies, Returns, and Value Behavior

Dependent values may survive transfers and calls only if the required anchors and rights remain valid. Second-class access does not imply an arbitrary persistent reference.

## 79. Non-Escaping Values and Returns

----
## 86. Arena, Active Views, and Reset

Two disjoint issued regions may be used simultaneously with valid derived rights. `reset` is rejected while an issuance or active dependency would make recycling unsafe; after a legal end of use for all the relevant blocks, the region may be reissued. Reissuance modifies neither the bytes nor the initialization state. A read remains subject to the ordinary conditions of the memory model, notably `Init`, access rights, and representation validity for the requested type. Spec 4 will determine the construction and typing obligations of reissued values.

230	  /-- §77.2: local self-blocking prevention, `destination` is not in `region`. -/
231	  dstNotIn : dst ∉ region

233	/-- Decidability of `IssueStatic` (§77). -/
234	instance (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) :
235	    Decidable (IssueStatic s E region dst) :=
236	  decidable_of_iff (s.Active E.internal ∧ MetaRight s E ∧
237	    (∀ l ∈ region, l ∈ footprint s.P E.storage) ∧ s.Usable dst ∧ isLeaf s.P dst ∧
238	    (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length,
239	      OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun z => z.active = true → z.holder ≠ .place dst) True) ∧
240	    HasRight s .modify dst ∧ dst ∉ region)
241	    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h⟩,
242	     fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h⟩⟩
243	
244	/-- §77.5: the effective mode of `internal` permits `Modify` on every leaf of the region. -/
245	def IssueRight (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) : Prop :=
246	  ∀ l ∈ region, Allows (effective s E.internal l) .modify
247	
248	/-- Decidability of `IssueRight` (§77.5). -/
249	instance (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) : Decidable (IssueRight s E region) := by
250	  unfold IssueRight; infer_instance
251	
252	/-- Kernel part of the effect of `issue` (§77, `ok` effect): a block authority of fresh identity
253	`|A|`, derived from `internal`, of mode `Modify`, on the region, held by `destination`, which
254	receives the corresponding anchor; only leaf `destination` becomes `Init`. -/
255	def issueKEff (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : S3 :=
256	  { s with
257	    A := s.A ++ [⟨.modify, some E.internal, region, .place dst, true⟩]
258	    D := fun q => if q = dst then s.D dst ++ [s.A.length] else s.D q
259	    I := fun l => if l = dst then .init else s.I l }
260	
261	/-- Metadata part of the effect of `issue` (§77, `ok` effect; §46): the leaves of the region leave
262	`available`; the issuance joins `issued` with its authority. -/
263	def issueMeta (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) : ArenaEntry :=
264	  { E with
265	    available := E.available.filter fun l => decide (l ∉ region)
266	    issued := (region, s.A.length) :: E.issued }

268	/-- Checks of `issue` on the simulated resulting state (§77.3, §77.6). -/
269	structure IssueArrival (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : Prop where
270	  /-- §77.3: `AnchorOrder` for the new anchor of `destination`, in the resulting state. -/
271	  anchorOrder : EffAnchorOK (issueKEff s E region dst) s.A.length
272	    ((issueKEff s E region dst).pframe dst)
273	  /-- §77.6: `AnchorOrderHeld` in the resulting state. -/
274	  anchorOrderHeld : AnchorOrderHeld (issueKEff s E region dst)
275	  /-- §77.6, O8.5: `destination` remains under exercisable `Modify` in the resulting state. -/
276	  keepsDst : HasRight (issueKEff s E region dst) .modify dst
277	
278	/-- Decidability of `IssueArrival` (§77). -/
279	instance (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) :
280	    Decidable (IssueArrival s E region dst) :=
281	  decidable_of_iff (EffAnchorOK (issueKEff s E region dst) s.A.length
282	      ((issueKEff s E region dst).pframe dst) ∧ AnchorOrderHeld (issueKEff s E region dst) ∧
283	    HasRight (issueKEff s E region dst) .modify dst)
284	    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c⟩ => ⟨a, b, c⟩, fun ⟨a, b, c⟩ => ⟨a, b, c⟩⟩
285	
286	/-- Library state after an `ok` issue of entry `i` (§77, `ok` effect). -/
287	def issueL (L : LState) (i : Nat) (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : LState :=
288	  ⟨issueKEff L.kern E region dst, L.arenas.set i (issueMeta L.kern E region)⟩
289	
290	/-- The contract of `issue` on entry `i` (§77, §58): `reject` when the entry is missing or a
291	static precondition fails; `fail`, the state unchanged, when the region is unavailable (§77.4);
292	`reject` when the effective right (§77.5) or a check on the resulting state (§77.3, §77.6)
293	fails; `ok` otherwise. -/
294	inductive IssueC (i : Nat) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) (L : LState) :
295	    Outcome3 LState → Prop where
296	  | noEntry : L.arenas[i]? = none → IssueC i region dst L .reject
297	  | static {E : ArenaEntry} : L.arenas[i]? = some E → ¬ IssueStatic L.kern E region dst →
298	      IssueC i region dst L .reject
299	  | fail {E : ArenaEntry} : L.arenas[i]? = some E → IssueStatic L.kern E region dst →
300	      ¬ Avail E region → IssueC i region dst L .fail
301	  | noRight {E : ArenaEntry} : L.arenas[i]? = some E → IssueStatic L.kern E region dst →
302	      Avail E region → ¬ IssueRight L.kern E region → IssueC i region dst L .reject
303	  | noArrival {E : ArenaEntry} : L.arenas[i]? = some E → IssueStatic L.kern E region dst →
304	      Avail E region → IssueRight L.kern E region → ¬ IssueArrival L.kern E region dst →
305	      IssueC i region dst L .reject
306	  | ok {E : ArenaEntry} : L.arenas[i]? = some E → IssueStatic L.kern E region dst →
307	      Avail E region → IssueRight L.kern E region → IssueArrival L.kern E region dst →
308	      IssueC i region dst L (.ok (issueL L i E region dst))
309	
310	/-- `issue` as a derived operation (Part XIV, §77): its static checks, then the availability
311	`fail` (§77.4), then `split` of `internal` on the region (O2) and `store` of the block, of fresh
312	identity `|A|`, into the destination (O8); the metadata is updated on `ok`. -/
313	inductive IssueD (k : K) (i : Nat) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) (L : LState) :
314	    Outcome3 LState → Prop where
315	  | noEntry : L.arenas[i]? = none → IssueD k i region dst L .reject
316	  | static {E : ArenaEntry} : L.arenas[i]? = some E → ¬ IssueStatic L.kern E region dst →
317	      IssueD k i region dst L .reject
318	  | fail {E : ArenaEntry} : L.arenas[i]? = some E → IssueStatic L.kern E region dst →
319	      ¬ Avail E region → IssueD k i region dst L .fail
320	  | split {E : ArenaEntry} : L.arenas[i]? = some E → IssueStatic L.kern E region dst →
321	      Avail E region → SplitStep k E.internal [region] L.kern .reject →
322	      IssueD k i region dst L .reject
323	  | store {E : ArenaEntry} {s₁ : S3} : L.arenas[i]? = some E → IssueStatic L.kern E region dst →
324	      Avail E region → SplitStep k E.internal [region] L.kern (.ok s₁) →
325	      StoreStep L.kern.A.length dst s₁ .reject → IssueD k i region dst L .reject
326	  | ok {E : ArenaEntry} {s₁ s₂ : S3} : L.arenas[i]? = some E →
327	      IssueStatic L.kern E region dst → Avail E region →
328	      SplitStep k E.internal [region] L.kern (.ok s₁) →
329	      StoreStep L.kern.A.length dst s₁ (.ok s₂) →
330	      IssueD k i region dst L (.ok ⟨s₂, L.arenas.set i (issueMeta L.kern E region)⟩)

332	/-! ## O19 `reset` (§78) -/
333	
334	/-- §78.3: no still-usable place depends on an anchor in the strict origin subtree of
335	`internal`. Dependencies of contained values are covered since parts are places. -/
336	def ResetNoDeps (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) : Prop :=
337	  ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, s.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, E.internal ∉ s.ancs x
338	
339	/-- Decidability of `ResetNoDeps` (§78.3). -/
340	instance (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) : Decidable (ResetNoDeps s E) := by
341	  unfold ResetNoDeps; infer_instance
342	
343	/-- Preconditions of `reset(arena)` (§78). "`internal` and the arena's other restrictions remain
344	valid" (§78.1) and "validity obligations of other nested arenas remain satisfied" (§78.3) name no
345	checkable condition beyond `ArenaInv` and are not represented. -/
346	structure ResetPre (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) : Prop where
347	  /-- §78.1: the entry is live. -/
348	  live : s.Active E.internal
349	  /-- §78.1: `MetaRight`, exercisable `Modify` over the arena value (§36). -/
350	  metaRight : MetaRight s E
351	  /-- §78.2: no active authority derived from `internal` covers a leaf of the storage. -/
352	  noCover : ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, E.internal ∈ s.ancs j → s.Active j →
353	    ∀ l ∈ s.afp j, l ∉ footprint s.P E.storage
354	  /-- §78.3: no usable place depends on an anchor in the strict origin subtree of `internal`. -/
355	  noDeps : ResetNoDeps s E
356	
357	/-- Decidability of `ResetPre` (§78). -/
358	instance (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) : Decidable (ResetPre s E) :=
359	  decidable_of_iff (s.Active E.internal ∧ MetaRight s E ∧
360	    (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, E.internal ∈ s.ancs j → s.Active j →
361	      ∀ l ∈ s.afp j, l ∉ footprint s.P E.storage) ∧ ResetNoDeps s E)
362	    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c, d⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d⟩, fun ⟨a, b, c, d⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d⟩⟩
363	
364	/-- Kernel part of the effect of `reset` (§78 `ok` effect, Part XIV): the record of the `Modify`
365	derivation of `internal` over all the storage, already released; no leaf becomes `Init`. -/
366	def resetKEff (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) : S3 :=
367	  { s with A := s.A ++ [⟨.modify, some E.internal, footprint s.P E.storage, .frame s.top, false⟩] }
368	
369	/-- Metadata part of the effect of `reset` (§78 `ok` effect, §46): all leaves of the storage
370	become available; `issued` is cleared. -/
371	def resetMeta (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) : ArenaEntry :=
372	  { E with available := footprint s.P E.storage, issued := [] }
373	
374	/-- Library state after an `ok` reset of entry `i` (§78). -/
375	def resetL (L : LState) (i : Nat) (E : ArenaEntry) : LState :=
376	  ⟨resetKEff L.kern E, L.arenas.set i (resetMeta L.kern E)⟩
377	
378	/-- The contract of `reset` on entry `i` (§78, §58): `ok` when the entry exists and the
379	preconditions hold, `reject` otherwise. -/
380	inductive ResetC (i : Nat) (L : LState) : Outcome3 LState → Prop where
381	  | noEntry : L.arenas[i]? = none → ResetC i L .reject
382	  | reject {E : ArenaEntry} : L.arenas[i]? = some E → ¬ ResetPre L.kern E → ResetC i L .reject
383	  | ok {E : ArenaEntry} : L.arenas[i]? = some E → ResetPre L.kern E →
384	      ResetC i L (.ok (resetL L i E))
385	
386	/-- `reset` as a derived operation (Part XIV, §78): `derive` of `internal` at `Modify` over the
387	footprint of the storage (O1), `release` of the derived authority (O3), then the explicit contract
388	check of §78.3; the metadata is updated on `ok`. -/
389	inductive ResetD (i : Nat) (L : LState) : Outcome3 LState → Prop where
390	  | noEntry : L.arenas[i]? = none → ResetD i L .reject
391	  | derive {E : ArenaEntry} : L.arenas[i]? = some E →
392	      DeriveStep E.internal (footprint L.kern.P E.storage) .modify L.kern .reject →
393	      ResetD i L .reject
394	  | release {E : ArenaEntry} {s₁ : S3} : L.arenas[i]? = some E →
395	      DeriveStep E.internal (footprint L.kern.P E.storage) .modify L.kern (.ok s₁) →
396	      ReleaseStep L.kern.A.length s₁ .reject → ResetD i L .reject
397	  | contract {E : ArenaEntry} {s₁ s₂ : S3} : L.arenas[i]? = some E →
398	      DeriveStep E.internal (footprint L.kern.P E.storage) .modify L.kern (.ok s₁) →
399	      ReleaseStep L.kern.A.length s₁ (.ok s₂) → ¬ ResetNoDeps L.kern E → ResetD i L .reject
400	  | ok {E : ArenaEntry} {s₁ s₂ : S3} : L.arenas[i]? = some E →
401	      DeriveStep E.internal (footprint L.kern.P E.storage) .modify L.kern (.ok s₁) →
402	      ReleaseStep L.kern.A.length s₁ (.ok s₂) → ResetNoDeps L.kern E →
403	      ResetD i L (.ok ⟨s₂, L.arenas.set i (resetMeta L.kern E)⟩)

407	/-- `Allows` at `Modify` is effective `Modify` (§43). -/
408	theorem allows_modify_iff {e : Option Mode} : Allows e .modify ↔ e = some .modify := by
409	  cases e with
410	  | none => simp [Allows, OptP]
411	  | some m => cases m <;> simp [Allows, OptP, Mode.le]

413	/-- Effective `Modify` permits every requested mode (§43: `Observe ≤ Modify`). -/
414	theorem allows_some_modify (m : Mode) : Allows (some .modify) m := by
415	  cases m <;> simp [Allows, OptP, Mode.le]

417	/-- An exercisable authority exists (§43). -/
418	theorem exercisable_lt {s : S3} {a : Nat} {m : Mode} (h : s.ExercisableAt a m) :
419	    a < s.A.length := by
420	  cases h <;> exact lt_of_getElem? ‹_›

420	  cases h <;> exact lt_of_getElem? ‹_›

422	/-- An exercise at `Modify` is an exercise at every mode (§43: `Observe ≤ Modify`). -/
423	theorem exercisable_of_modify {s : S3} {a : Nat} {m : Mode} (h : s.ExercisableAt a .modify) :
424	    s.ExercisableAt a m := by
425	  generalize hm : Mode.modify = m' at h
426	  induction h with
427	  | base hy ha hle hf =>
428	    subst hm
429	    exact .base hy ha (.inr (hle.resolve_left (by decide))) hf
430	  | held hy ha hle hp _ hc ih =>
431	    subst hm
432	    exact .held hy ha (.inr (hle.resolve_left (by decide))) hp (ih rfl)
433	      fun l hl => by rw [allows_modify_iff.1 (hc l hl)]; exact allows_some_modify m

435	/-- A permitted effective mode comes from an existing authority covering the leaf (§43,
436	case 1). -/
437	theorem mem_of_allows {s : S3} {a l : Nat} {m : Mode} (h : Allows (effective s a l) m) :
438	    ∃ x, s.A[a]? = some x ∧ l ∈ x.footprint := by
439	  unfold effective at h
440	  cases hx : s.A[a]? with
441	  | none => rw [hx] at h; exact h.elim
442	  | some x =>
443	    rw [hx] at h; simp only at h
444	    split at h
445	    · exact ⟨x, rfl, ‹_ ∧ _›.2⟩
446	    · exact h.elim

448	/-- More covering descendants permit no more (§43, cases 2–4). -/
449	theorem allows_effOf_append {m m' : Mode} {ds e : List Mode}
450	    (h : Allows (effOf m (ds ++ e)) m') : Allows (effOf m ds) m' := by
451	  by_cases h0 : ds ++ e = []
452	  · rw [(List.append_eq_nil_iff.1 h0).1]; simpa [effOf, h0] using h
453	  · by_cases h1 : Mode.modify ∈ ds ++ e
454	    · simp [effOf, h0, h1, Allows, OptP] at h
455	    · have hm' : m' = .observe := by
456	        cases m' with
457	        | observe => rfl
458	        | modify => simp [effOf, h0, h1, Allows, OptP, Mode.le] at h
459	      subst hm'
460	      have h1' : Mode.modify ∉ ds := fun h' => h1 (List.mem_append_left _ h')
461	      by_cases hd : ds = []
462	      · simp [effOf, hd, Allows, OptP, Mode.le]
463	      · simp [effOf, hd, h1', Allows, OptP, Mode.le]

465	/-- Adding an authority only takes effective modes away from the existing ones (§43,
466	case 3). -/
467	theorem allows_addAuth_back {s : S3} {y₀ : Authority} {b l : Nat} {m : Mode}
468	    (hb : b < s.A.length) (h : Allows (effective (s.addAuth y₀) b l) m) :
469	    Allows (effective s b l) m := by
470	  unfold effective at h ⊢
471	  rw [addAuth_lt hb, descModes_addAuth] at h
472	  cases hx : s.A[b]? with
473	  | none => rw [hx] at h; exact h
474	  | some x =>
475	    rw [hx] at h; simp only at h ⊢
476	    split at h
477	    · rename_i hc; simp only [hc, and_self, ite_true]; exact allows_effOf_append h
478	    · exact h.elim

480	/-- Exercise after adding the block `y₀` of `src`, for a former authority, comes from an
481	exercise before: a link through the block is replaced by a link through `src` (§43). -/
482	theorem exercisable_addAuth_back {s : S3} {y₀ : Authority} {src : Nat}
483	    (hsrc : s.ExercisableAt src .modify)
484	    (hfp : ∀ l ∈ y₀.footprint, effective s src l = some .modify) {a : Nat} {m : Mode}
485	    (h : (s.addAuth y₀).ExercisableAt a m) : a < s.A.length → s.ExercisableAt a m := by
486	  induction h with
487	  | base hy ha hle hf =>
488	    intro hlt
489	    rw [addAuth_lt hlt] at hy
490	    exact .base hy ha hle hf
491	  | @held a' p b m' y hy ha hle hp hb hc ih =>
492	    intro hlt
493	    rw [addAuth_lt hlt] at hy
494	    by_cases hbl : b < s.A.length
495	    · exact .held hy ha hle hp (ih hbl) fun l hl => allows_addAuth_back hbl (hc l hl)
496	    · have hbe : b = s.A.length := by
497	        have := exercisable_lt hb; simp [S3.addAuth] at this; omega
498	      subst hbe
499	      refine .held hy ha hle hp (exercisable_of_modify hsrc) fun l hl => ?_
500	      obtain ⟨x, hx, hlx⟩ := mem_of_allows (hc l hl)
501	      rw [addAuth_self] at hx; cases hx
502	      rw [hfp l hlx]; exact allows_some_modify m'

504	/-- `HasRight` after adding the block `y₀` of `src`, on a place none of whose leaves the block
505	covers, comes from `HasRight` before (§43). -/
506	theorem hasRight_addAuth_back {s : S3} {y₀ : Authority} {src p : Nat} {m : Mode}
507	    (hsrc : s.ExercisableAt src .modify)
508	    (hfp : ∀ l ∈ y₀.footprint, effective s src l = some .modify)
509	    (hout : ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P p, l ∉ y₀.footprint) (h : HasRight (s.addAuth y₀) m p) :
510	    HasRight s m p := by
511	  obtain ⟨a, -, ha, hall⟩ := h
512	  by_cases hlt : a < s.A.length
513	  · exact ⟨a, List.mem_range.2 hlt, exercisable_addAuth_back hsrc hfp ha hlt,
514	      fun l hl => allows_addAuth_back hlt (hall l hl)⟩
515	  · have hae : a = s.A.length := by
516	      have := exercisable_lt ha; simp [S3.addAuth] at this; omega
517	    subst hae
518	    refine ⟨src, List.mem_range.2 (exercisable_lt hsrc), exercisable_of_modify hsrc,
519	      fun l hl => ?_⟩
520	    obtain ⟨x, hx, hlx⟩ := mem_of_allows (hall l hl)
521	    rw [addAuth_self] at hx; cases hx
522	    exact absurd hlx (hout l hl)

524	/-- The effect of `store` on an existing authority (§65, `ok` effect). -/

527	      A := s.A.set a { y with holder := .place p }
528	      D := fun q => if q = p then s.D p ++ [a] else s.D q
529	      I := fun l => if l = p then .init else s.I l } := by

535	  · rename_i y hy
536	    refine ⟨by simp, fun j => ?_⟩
537	    by_cases hj : a = j
538	    · subst hj; rw [List.getElem?_set_self (lt_of_getElem? hy), hy]; rfl
539	    · rw [List.getElem?_set_ne hj]

543	from the current frame to a place (§43, §65). -/

545	    (hh : y.holder = .frame s.top) {b : Nat} {m : Mode}
546	    (h : (storeEff s a p).ExercisableAt b m) : s.ExercisableAt b m := by

552	  have hal := lt_of_getElem? hy

557	      rw [hA, List.getElem?_set_self hal] at hz; cases hz
558	      simp at hf

565	      exact .base hy za hle hh
566	    · rw [hA, List.getElem?_set_ne hba] at hz
567	      exact .held hz za hle hq ih fun l hl => by rw [← he]; exact hc l (by rw [hP]; exact hl)

570	theorem hasRight_store_back {s : S3} {a p q : Nat} {y : Authority} {m : Mode}

572	    HasRight s m q := by

import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Ops

/-!
# Access kernel: invariants, initial state, reachability

Invariants of `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md`: `WF3` (§49), `I1`–`I4` (§50–§53),
`NoDangling` and `NoOrphan` (§54), `Inv3` and `I5` (§57), the declared statics and `S3.init`
(§47), `StaticPinnedBottom` (§75), and reachability from `S3.init statics` under the kernel steps
O1–O16 (§57). `AnchorOrder` and `AnchorOrderHeld` (§44) are in
`Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Basic`, since operations read them.
-/

namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Access

/-! ## Root places and root authorities (§40, §49) -/

/-- Root place (§40): an existing place with no structural parent. -/
def RootPlace (P : List Place) (r : Nat) : Prop := r < P.length ∧ parentOf P r = none

/-- Decidability of `RootPlace` (§40). -/
instance (P : List Place) (r : Nat) : Decidable (RootPlace P r) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (_ ∧ _))

/-- `RootChain` (§49.6): the origin chain of an authority covering a leaf ends at a root
authority (no origin) whose footprint is the footprint of a root place containing that leaf. -/
def RootChain (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ (a : Nat) (y : Authority) (l : Nat), s.A[a]? = some y → l ∈ y.footprint → isLeaf s.P l →
    ∃ x z r, (x = a ∨ x ∈ s.ancs a) ∧ s.A[x]? = some z ∧ z.origin = none ∧ RootPlace s.P r ∧
      partOf s.P l r ∧ ∀ l', l' ∈ z.footprint ↔ l' ∈ footprint s.P r

/-- `RootHeld` (§49.7, §40): every usable root place has an active root authority of own mode
`Modify`, with no origin, held by the owner of the place, whose footprint is the footprint of the
place. -/
def RootHeld (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ r, RootPlace s.P r → s.Usable r → ∃ (i : Nat) (z : Authority) (pr : Place),
    s.A[i]? = some z ∧ z.active = true ∧ z.origin = none ∧ z.mode = .modify ∧
    s.P[r]? = some pr ∧ z.holder = pr.owner ∧ ∀ l, l ∈ z.footprint ↔ l ∈ footprint s.P r

/-- Auxiliary converse of `RootHeld` (§40, §49.7), not a clause of `WF3`: an authority with no
origin is held by the owner of the root place of every leaf it covers. -/
def RootHeldConv (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ (x : Nat) (z : Authority) (l r : Nat), s.A[x]? = some z → z.origin = none → l ∈ z.footprint →
    RootPlace s.P r → partOf s.P l r → ∃ pr, s.P[r]? = some pr ∧ z.holder = pr.owner

/-! ## `WF3` (§49) -/

/-- `WF3(s)` (§49): one field per item of §49. Index order of parents and origins represents
acyclicity (§49, last paragraph). -/

import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Preserve.Common

/-!
# Arenas: the reference library abstraction (Part XIV)

Arenas of `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md`, Part XIV (§76–§78), with §36, §46, §55,
§56, §58, §79, §86 and §88. An arena is a library abstraction (Part XIV): its entries live in a
library state separate from the kernel state `S₃` (§38, §46). `newArena` (O17) only registers an
entry; `issue` (O18) and `reset` (O19) are defined twice:

* as their contracts, clause by clause (§77, §78): `IssueC`, `ResetC`;
* as derived operations over the kernel steps (Part XIV): `issue` is its static checks, the
  availability `fail`, then `split` of `internal` on the region and `store` of the block into the
  destination (`IssueD`); `reset` is `derive` of `internal` at `Modify` over the whole storage,
  then `release`, then the explicit check of §78.3 (`ResetD`).

`issue_as_kernel` and `reset_as_kernel` show that both definitions have the same outcomes and the
same arrival states. Library reachability (`LReach`, `LReachNG`) uses the derived operations, so
its kernel states are kernel-reachable (`newArena_as_library`).
-/

/-! ## Witnesses on library-reachable states (§78.3, §86, §55, §63)

Runs from `LState.init Examples.st` (§47: static leaves 0 `Init`, 1 and 2 `Uninit`, with root
authorities 0, 1 and 2 held by frame 0) under the test contract `Examples.K0`. In the runs for
§78.3 and §86, leaf 0 is the arena value, leaf 1 the storage, leaf 2 the destination. Every
precondition is decided by `decide`; `KInv ∧ KAux` of the final states is decided through
`KInvB`. -/

namespace Witness

open Examples

/-- Initial library state (§47). -/
def w0 : LState := LState.init st
/-- `derive(1, [1], Modify)`: authority 3 on the storage leaf, held by frame 0 (§60). -/
def w1 : LState := ⟨deriveEff w0.kern 1 [1] .modify, w0.arenas⟩
/-- `store(3, 0)`: authority 3 becomes `internal`, held by the arena value 0 (§65). -/
def w2 : LState := ⟨storeEff w1.kern 3 0, w1.arenas⟩
/-- `newArena(1, 3)` (§76). -/
def w3 : LState := newArenaEff w2 1 3
/-- The entry registered by `newArena(1, 3)` (§46, §76). -/
def wE : ArenaEntry := ⟨1, 3, [1], []⟩

/-- The common prefix is library-reachable (Part XIV, §76). -/
theorem w3_reach : LReach K0 st w3 := by
  have r1 : LReach K0 st w1 := .step .init (.kernel (.derive (.ok (by decide))))
  have r2 : LReach K0 st w2 := .step r1 (.kernel (.store (.ok (by decide))))
  exact .step r2 (.newArena (others := []) (.ok (by decide)))

/-- `issue(0, [1], 2)`: `split(3, [[1]])` then `store(4, 2)` (§77). -/
def r4 : LState :=
  ⟨storeEff (splitEff w3.kern 3 [[1]]) w3.kern.A.length 2,
    w3.arenas.set 0 (issueMeta w3.kern wE [1])⟩
/-- `write(4, [1])`: the storage leaf 1 is written through block 4 (§67). -/
def r5 : LState := ⟨write3Eff r4.kern [1], r4.arenas⟩
/-- `endUse(2)`: the destination ends; block 4, held by it, is released (§69). -/
def r6 : LState := ⟨endUseEff r5.kern 2, r5.arenas⟩
/-- The entry after the first issue (§77 `ok` effect). -/
def rE : ArenaEntry := ⟨1, 3, [], [([1], 4)]⟩
/-- `reset(0)`: `derive(3, [1], Modify)`, `release(5)`, metadata restored (§78). -/
def r7 : LState :=
  ⟨releaseEff (deriveEff r6.kern 3 (footprint r6.kern.P 1) .modify) r6.kern.A.length,
    r6.arenas.set 0 (resetMeta r6.kern rE)⟩
/-- The entry after the reset (§78 `ok` effect). -/
def rE' : ArenaEntry := ⟨1, 3, [1], []⟩
/-- `issue(0, [1], 2)` again: `split(3, [[1]])` then `store(6, 2)` (§77). -/
def r8 : LState :=
  ⟨storeEff (splitEff r7.kern 3 [[1]]) r7.kern.A.length 2,
    r7.arenas.set 0 (issueMeta r7.kern rE' [1])⟩

/-- **§86: a reissued block reads a former value** (spec problem). Leaf 1 is `Uninit` when it is
first issued, is written through block 4, keeps `Init` across `endUse` of the destination, the
legal `reset` (§78: "No leaf is made `Init` by `reset`", and no leaf is made `Uninit` either) and
the reissue, which initializes only the destination 2 (§77). In the final library-reachable state,
which satisfies `KInv ∧ KAux`, `read` of leaf 1 through the new block 6 is `ok` (§66.1 asks only
that the leaf be `Init`): the reissued block reads the value written under the former issuance,
with no initialization of it after the reissue. This contradicts §86, "Reissuance does not permit
reading a former logical value without the required initialization". -/
theorem reissue_reads_former_value :
    LReach K0 st r8 ∧ KInv r8.kern ∧ KAux r8.kern ∧
    r4.kern.I 1 = .uninit ∧ r5.kern.I 1 = .init ∧ r7.kern.I 1 = .init ∧ r8.kern.I 1 = .init ∧
    ¬ r8.kern.Active 4 ∧
    (r8.kern.A[6]?).map (fun y => (y.origin, y.footprint, y.holder, y.active)) =
      some (some 3, [1], .place 2, true) ∧
    r8.arenas = [⟨1, 3, [], [([1], 6)]⟩] ∧
    Read3Step 6 [1] r8.kern (.ok r8.kern) := by
  have h4 : LReach K0 st r4 := .step w3_reach
    (.issue (i := 0) (region := [1]) (dst := 2)
      (.ok (E := wE) (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (.ok (by decide)) (.ok (by decide))))
  have h5 : LReach K0 st r5 := .step h4 (.kernel (.write (a := 4) (.ok (by decide))))
  have h6 : LReach K0 st r6 := .step h5 (.kernel (.endUse (.ok (by decide))))
  have h7 : LReach K0 st r7 := .step h6
    (.reset (i := 0) (.ok (E := rE) (by decide) (.ok (by decide)) (.ok (by decide)) (by decide)))
  have h8 : LReach K0 st r8 := .step h7
    (.issue (i := 0) (region := [1]) (dst := 2)
      (.ok (E := rE') (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (.ok (by decide)) (.ok (by decide))))
  have hk := KInvB.sound (s := r8.kern) (by decide)
  exact ⟨h8, hk.1, hk.2, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide,
    by decide, .ok (by decide)⟩

end Witness

end Ern.MemoryModel.Arena

81	
82	/-- `ArenaInv` (§55), required for live arenas. "Still-issued" is read as "with an active block
83	authority". The clause "anchor and ownership restrictions are respected" has no referent and is
84	not represented; "complying with exclusivity and validity rules" is left to the kernel
85	invariants (§57). -/
86	structure ArenaInv (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) : Prop where
87	  /-- §55, item 1: `storage` designates an existing, usable place. -/
88	  storageUsable : s.Usable E.storage
89	  /-- §55, item 1: the footprint of `internal` is exactly the footprint of `storage`. -/
90	  fpEq : ∀ l, l ∈ s.afp E.internal ↔ l ∈ footprint s.P E.storage
91	  /-- §55, item 2: `internal` is active. -/
92	  active : s.Active E.internal

94	  shape : OptP (s.A[E.internal]?) (fun y => y.mode = .modify ∧ y.holder.isPlace = true) False
95	  /-- §55, item 3: available leaves belong to the administered storage. -/
96	  availableIn : ∀ l ∈ E.available, l ∈ footprint s.P E.storage
97	  /-- §55, item 3: issued regions belong to the administered storage. -/
98	  issuedIn : ∀ e ∈ E.issued, ∀ l ∈ e.1, l ∈ footprint s.P E.storage

101	    ∀ l ∈ e.1, l ∉ e'.1
102	  /-- §55, item 4: no leaf of a still-issued region belongs to `available`. -/
103	  notAvailable : ∀ e ∈ E.issued, s.Active e.2 → ∀ l ∈ e.1, l ∉ E.available

/-- Decidability of `WF3` (§49), through its bounded check. -/
instance (s : S3) : Decidable (WF3 s) := decidable_of_iff _ wf3_iff_kb.symm

/-- `I1` (§50) is its bounded check. -/
theorem i1_iff_kb {s : S3} : I1 s ↔ KB_i1 s := by
  constructor
  · intro h1 a _ b _
    cases hx : s.A[a]? with
    | none => trivial
    | some x =>
      show OptP (s.A[b]?) _ True
      cases hy : s.A[b]? with
      | none => trivial
      | some y =>
        intro hab xa ya ⟨p, hpx, hpy⟩ hba hab'
        exact h1 a b x y p hab hx hy xa ya hpx hpy hba hab'
  · intro h a b x y p hab hx hy xa ya hpx hpy hab' hba
    have := h a (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hx)) b (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hy))
    rw [hx] at this; simp only [OptP, hy] at this
    exact this hab xa ya ⟨p, hpx, hpy⟩ hab' hba

/-- Decidability of `I1` (§50), through its bounded check. -/
instance (s : S3) : Decidable (I1 s) := decidable_of_iff _ i1_iff_kb.symm

/-- `KInv ∧ KAux` with bounded quantifiers (§49–§54, §57; decision procedure). -/

  frames : KB_frames s
  /-- §49.2. -/
  places : KB_places s
  /-- §49.3. -/
  owners : KB_owners s
  /-- §49.4. -/
  footprints : KB_footprints s
  /-- §49.5. -/
  origins : KB_origins s
  /-- §49.6. -/
  rootChain : KB_rootChain s
  /-- §49.7. -/
  rootHeld : KB_rootHeld s
  /-- §49.8. -/
  holders : KB_holders s
  /-- §50. -/
  i1 : KB_i1 s
  /-- §51. -/
  i2 : KB_i2 s
  /-- §52. -/
  i3 : KB_i3 s
  /-- §44. -/
  anchorOrder : KB_anchorOrder s
  /-- §54, `NoDangling`. -/
  noDangling : KB_noDangling s
  /-- §44. -/
  anchorOrderHeld : KB_anchorOrderHeld s
  /-- `RootHeldConv` (§40, §49.7). -/
  rootHeldConv : KB_rootHeldConv s

/-- Decidability of `KInvB` (decision procedure for §49–§54, §57). -/
instance (s : S3) : Decidable (KInvB s) :=
  decidable_of_iff (KB_frames s ∧ KB_places s ∧ KB_owners s ∧ KB_footprints s ∧ KB_origins s ∧
    KB_rootChain s ∧ KB_rootHeld s ∧ KB_holders s ∧ KB_i1 s ∧ KB_i2 s ∧ KB_i3 s ∧
    KB_anchorOrder s ∧ KB_noDangling s ∧ KB_anchorOrderHeld s ∧ KB_rootHeldConv s)
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, j, l, m, n, o, q⟩ =>
      ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, j, l, m, n, o, q⟩,
     fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, j, l, m, n, o, q⟩ =>
      ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, i, j, l, m, n, o, q⟩⟩

/-- Soundness of `KInvB` (decision procedure for §49–§54, §57): it gives `KInv ∧ KAux`. -/

  have hw : WF3 s := wf3_iff_kb.2 ⟨h.frames, h.places, h.owners, h.footprints, h.origins,

    fun x z l r hz hzo hl hr hlr => ?_⟩
  · have := h.i2 b (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hy))
    rw [hy] at this; simp only [OptP, ho] at this
    cases hxa : s.A[a]? with
    | none => rw [hxa] at this; exact this.elim
    | some x => rw [hxa] at this; exact ⟨x, rfl, this⟩
  · have := h.noDangling j (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hy))
    rw [hy] at this
    exact this ya q (List.mem_range.2 (footprint_lt hl)) hq l hl hly
  · have := h.rootHeldConv x (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hz))
    rw [hz] at this
    have h' := this hzo l hl r (List.mem_range.2 hr.1) hr hlr
    cases hp : s.P[r]? with
    | none => rw [hp] at h'; exact h'.elim
    | some pr => rw [hp] at h'; exact ⟨pr, rfl, h'⟩

theorem noCover_of_derive {s : S3} {E : ArenaEntry}
    (hd : DerivePre s E.internal (footprint s.P E.storage) .modify) :
    ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, E.internal ∈ s.ancs j → s.Active j →
      ∀ l ∈ s.afp j, l ∉ footprint s.P E.storage := by
  intro j _ ha hja l hl hls
  obtain ⟨y, hy, ya⟩ := hja
  have hly : l ∈ y.footprint := by simpa [S3.afp, hy] using hl
  exact no_desc_of_modify hy ya hly ha (allows_modify_iff.1 (hd.modeOK l hls))

/-- v0.1 §78.3, second sentence: under precondition 2 of §78 and invariant I3 (§52; a valid
anchor is an active one, §51), §78.3 holds. An anchor of a usable place is active (I3), so an
anchor in the strict origin subtree of `internal` covering a leaf of the storage would be an
active derivative of `internal` covering that leaf, which §78.2 excludes. -/
theorem resetNoDeps_of_noCover {s : S3} {E : ArenaEntry} (h3 : I3 s)
    (h2 : ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, E.internal ∈ s.ancs j → s.Active j →
      ∀ l ∈ s.afp j, l ∉ footprint s.P E.storage) : ResetNoDeps s E := by
  intro q _ hq x hx hix l hl hls

  exact h2 x (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hy)) hix ⟨y, hy, ya⟩ l hl hls

accepted `derive` of `internal` over the storage (v0.1 §78.3, second sentence;
`noCover_of_derive`, `resetNoDeps_of_noCover`): the derived `reset` is its kernel sequence. -/
theorem resetNoDeps_of_derive {s : S3} {E : ArenaEntry} (h3 : I3 s)
    (hd : DerivePre s E.internal (footprint s.P E.storage) .modify) : ResetNoDeps s E :=
  resetNoDeps_of_noCover h3 (noCover_of_derive hd)

exactly the preconditions of `derive` of `internal` at `Modify` over the storage (§60) and the
explicit check of §78.3: §78.1 is §60.1 (`metaRight_iff`; the origin chain of the active `internal`
is active by I2, §51), §78.2 is §60.2 (effective `Modify` on every leaf of the storage), §60.3
follows from I1. -/
theorem resetPre_iff {s : S3} {E : ArenaEntry} (hw : WF3 s) (h1 : I1 s) (h2 : I2 s)
    (hai : Live s E → ArenaInv s E) :
    ResetPre s E ↔
      DerivePre s E.internal (footprint s.P E.storage) .modify ∧ ResetNoDeps s E := by
  constructor
  · intro hp
    have hA := hai hp.live
    have hsh := hA.shape
    obtain ⟨yi, hyi, yia⟩ := hp.live
    rw [hyi] at hsh
    have hli : ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P E.storage, l ∈ yi.footprint := fun l hl => by
      have := (hA.fpEq l).2 hl; simpa [S3.afp, hyi] using this
    have hmod : ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P E.storage, Allows (effective s E.internal l) .modify := by
      intro l hl
      have hd : descModes s E.internal l = [] := by
        apply nil_of_forall_not_mem; intro e he
        obtain ⟨j, y, hy, ya, hly, hj, -⟩ := mem_descModes.1 he
        exact hp.noCover j (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hy)) hj ⟨y, hy, ya⟩ l

      rw [effective_eq hyi yia (hli l hl), hd]
      simp [effOf, hsh.1, Allows, OptP, Mode.le]
    refine ⟨⟨⟨yi, hyi, yia⟩, (metaRight_iff hA).1 hp.metaRight, h2.ancs_active ⟨yi, hyi, yia⟩,
      fun l hl => (mem_footprint.1 hl).elim fun h h' => ⟨h, h'.1⟩,
      fun l hl => (hA.fpEq l).2 hl, hmod, fun b _ => ?_, top_mem hw.frames.1⟩, hp.noDeps⟩
    unfold OptP; split
    · rename_i y hy
      rintro ya hb ⟨l, hl, hly⟩
      have hb1 : b ≠ E.internal := fun h => hb (h ▸ List.mem_cons_self ..)
      have hb2 : b ∉ s.ancs E.internal := fun h => hb (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ h)
      obtain ⟨h₁, h₂⟩ := new_vs_old h1 hyi yia (hli l hl) (hmod l hl) hy ya hly hb1 hb2
      exact ⟨h₂, h₁⟩

  · rintro ⟨hd, h3⟩
    have hA := hai hd.active
    exact ⟨hd.active, (metaRight_iff hA).2 hd.exercisable, noCover_of_derive hd, h3⟩

kernel invariant, when the entry satisfies `ArenaInv` if live, the contract of `reset` and the
derived operation (`derive` then `release`, then the explicit check of §78.3) have the same
outcomes, `ok` and `reject`, with the same arrival state, kernel part included (literal equality,
`resetKEff_eq`). On library-reachable states the hypotheses hold (`reset_as_kernel`). -/
theorem reset_as_kernel_of_inv {L : LState} {i : Nat} (hk : KInv L.kern)
    (hai : ∀ E, L.arenas[i]? = some E → Live L.kern E → ArenaInv L.kern E)
    (o : Outcome3 LState) : ResetC i L o ↔ ResetD i L o := by
  have hw := hk.1
  have h1 := hk.2.1.1.1
  have h2 := hk.2.1.1.2.1
  have h3 := hk.2.1.1.2.2.1

      (footprint L.kern.P E.storage) .modify) L.kern.A.length,
      L.arenas.set i (resetMeta L.kern E)⟩ := fun E => by
    rw [resetL, resetKEff_eq]
  constructor
  · intro h
    cases h with
    | noEntry h0 => exact .noEntry h0
    | @reject E hE hn =>
      have hiff := resetPre_iff hw h1 h2 (hai E hE)
      by_cases hd : DerivePre L.kern E.internal (footprint L.kern.P E.storage) .modify
      · exact .contract hE (.ok hd) (.ok (release_after_derive h3)) fun h3' => hn (hiff.2 ⟨hd, h3'⟩)
      · exact .derive hE (.reject hd)
    | @ok E hE hp =>
      obtain ⟨hd, h3'⟩ := (resetPre_iff hw h1 h2 (hai E hE)).1 hp
      rw [e E]
      exact .ok hE (.ok hd) (.ok (release_after_derive h3)) h3'
  · intro h
    cases h with
    | noEntry h0 => exact .noEntry h0
    | @derive E hE hd =>
      exact .reject hE fun hp =>
        Guarded.reject_iff.1 hd ((resetPre_iff hw h1 h2 (hai E hE)).1 hp).1
    | @release E s₁ hE hd hr =>
      obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hd
      exact absurd (release_after_derive h3) (Guarded.reject_iff.1 hr)
    | @contract E s₁ s₂ hE hd _ hn =>
      exact .reject hE fun hp => hn ((resetPre_iff hw h1 h2 (hai E hE)).1 hp).2
    | @ok E s₁ s₂ hE hd hr h3' =>
      obtain ⟨hd', rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hd
      obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hr
      rw [← e E]
      exact .ok hE ((resetPre_iff hw h1 h2 (hai E hE)).2 ⟨hd', h3'⟩)

/-- `reset` as its kernel sequence, per step (Part XIV, §78, §58): on a state satisfying the
kernel invariant, when the entry satisfies `ArenaInv` if live, the contract of `reset` and the
derived operation (`derive` then `release`, then the explicit check of §78.3) have the same
outcomes, `ok` and `reject`, with the same arrival state, kernel part included (literal equality,
`resetKEff_eq`). On library-reachable states the hypotheses hold (`reset_as_kernel`). -/
theorem reset_as_kernel_of_inv {L : LState} {i : Nat} (hk : KInv L.kern)
    (hai : ∀ E, L.arenas[i]? = some E → Live L.kern E → ArenaInv L.kern E)
    (o : Outcome3 LState) : ResetC i L o ↔ ResetD i L o := by
  have hw := hk.1
  have h1 := hk.2.1.1.1
  have h2 := hk.2.1.1.2.1
  have h3 := hk.2.1.1.2.2.1
  have e : ∀ E, resetL L i E = ⟨releaseEff (deriveEff L.kern E.internal
      (footprint L.kern.P E.storage) .modify) L.kern.A.length,
      L.arenas.set i (resetMeta L.kern E)⟩ := fun E => by
    rw [resetL, resetKEff_eq]
  constructor
  · intro h
    cases h with
    | noEntry h0 => exact .noEntry h0
    | @reject E hE hn =>
      have hiff := resetPre_iff hw h1 h2 (hai E hE)
      by_cases hd : DerivePre L.kern E.internal (footprint L.kern.P E.storage) .modify
      · exact .contract hE (.ok hd) (.ok (release_after_derive h3)) fun h3' => hn (hiff.2 ⟨hd, h3'⟩)
      · exact .derive hE (.reject hd)
    | @ok E hE hp =>
      obtain ⟨hd, h3'⟩ := (resetPre_iff hw h1 h2 (hai E hE)).1 hp
      rw [e E]
      exact .ok hE (.ok hd) (.ok (release_after_derive h3)) h3'
  · intro h
    cases h with
    | noEntry h0 => exact .noEntry h0
    | @derive E hE hd =>
      exact .reject hE fun hp =>
        Guarded.reject_iff.1 hd ((resetPre_iff hw h1 h2 (hai E hE)).1 hp).1
    | @release E s₁ hE hd hr =>
      obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hd
      exact absurd (release_after_derive h3) (Guarded.reject_iff.1 hr)
    | @contract E s₁ s₂ hE hd _ hn =>
      exact .reject hE fun hp => hn ((resetPre_iff hw h1 h2 (hai E hE)).1 hp).2
    | @ok E s₁ s₂ hE hd hr h3' =>
      obtain ⟨hd', rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hd
      obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hr
      rw [← e E]
      exact .ok hE ((resetPre_iff hw h1 h2 (hai E hE)).2 ⟨hd', h3'⟩)

{

  echo 'open Lean Elab Command in'

  echo '  let env ← getEnv'

    let mut all := 0

    for (n, ci) in env.constants.map₁.toList do

        if let .thmInfo _ := ci then thms := thms + 1
        let axs ← collectAxioms n
        let extra := axs.filter fun a => a != ``propext && a != ``Quot.sound
        if !extra.isEmpty then bad := bad.push (n, extra)
    IO.println s!"{modName}: constants {all}, theorems {thms}"

L
} > $F
